Let s break down the elements of the situation to understand it better.

In Pavlov s experiment, the meat is the unconditioned stimulus (UCS) because the meat is the normal, natural product that would cause saliva to flow in dogs. The flow of saliva is known as the unconditioned response (UCR) because that response occurs naturally with no learning.

UCS�(meat)------------------------------>(Unlearned)---------------------------->�UCR�(saliva flow)

When Pavlov rang a bell and then offered the dogs food, he was linking a conditioned stimulus (CS) to a conditioned response (CR). In other words, the dogs learned to associate a bell with food which is an unnatural response that must be learned. Bells do not automatically bring the idea of food to mind unless that association has been learned.

Some pet owners have noticed that dogs or cats hear the sound of an electric can opener (or the fridge door being opened) and associate that sound with feeding time because the bet is often given a can of food after that sound is heard.
